title: Cut non-essential expenses if cash flow is tight
summary: Streaming, restaurants, subscriptions, premium phone plans — if the budget doesn't balance, this is where to cut first.
detailsHtml:
The hierarchy of cuts

The first cuts should be subscription-based recurring charges that you don't actively use — they're the highest-yield reduction because they require no behavioral discipline once cancelled. Restaurants and convenience purchases come next; these are higher-friction because they require sustained habit change.

A note from r/personalfinance that holds up well: If you are dedicated to financial recovery, keep discretionary spending at an absolute minimum until high-interest debt is paid off. The math of high-interest debt is brutal enough that even modest discretionary cuts compound into substantial acceleration.
